title: rambling-runtime-todo-scratch - owen
content:
Quick brain dump / working todo log (aggressive stream-of-consciousness). Not for prod docs.

2026-03-11 -> 2026-03-13: context
- Oncall last night had two p99 spikes during a small internal perf test. Both align with micro-batching path + heavy redis eviction churn. Suspect mixing of eviction + cold KV load.
- Repro steps I used: local dev harness -> toy-model v2 (gpt-lite-7b), batch sizes [1,2,4,8], prefix caching enabled, synthetic traffic from loadgen 20 qps. Spike occurs reliably at batch 8 when kv_hit_rate < 35%.

Top TODOs (short):
1) Add detailed telemetry for KV miss origin: was it eviction or never-populated? (short-term: add a boolean tag kv_evicted_recently)
2) Experiment: throttle eviction frequency for LRU window to 2x current and measure p99. (owner: Mina)
3) Small code hygiene: audit places where cache.set is called without ttl argument -> default policy mismatch. (owner: me)
4) Prepare quick canary config to pin batch size <=6 for customer X (urgent)
5) Follow up on PR #812 (kernel scheduler backpressure) - ensure backpressure counters are exposed to console

Notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: eviction creates cold RPCs that spike latency when batch grows because the runtime tries to fill KV for all positions synchronously. That increases tail variability.
- Hypothesis B: scheduler mis-estimates effective concurrency when a bunch of requests trigger cold model slice loads (IO bound) -> spikes.

Quick instrumentation ideas (cheap):
- Emit kv.miss_reason tag: [evicted, not_found, truncated_cache] with sample rate 1:100 for initial pass.
- Add small histogram of kv.populate_time_ms (0..2000ms) keyed by model_shard.
- Capture batch_size_at_request and kv_hit_rate_at_request in trace span.

Ad-hoc notes from debugging session:
- Log snippet (approx):
  2026-03-12T02:14:02Z WARN runtime.kv_cache evict shard=3 evicted=128 total=4096
  2026-03-12T02:14:02Z INFO runtime.request id=abcd1234 batch=8 kv_hit_rate=0.29 populate_time_ms=812
  2026-03-12T02:14:02Z ERROR runtime.sched backpressure=true queue_len=34

Small experiment plan (this afternoon):
- Baseline: current master (no changes) with loadgen profile nightly-small (20qps, 75% short prompts). Record p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate distribution.
- Change A: disable eviction for shards 0..7 (in mem) -> run, record.
- Change B: set batch cap at 6 in router policy -> run.
- Change C: bump scheduler cpu_budget_scale by +0.2 (PR 812 tweak) -> run.

Open questions to ping SRE/infra:
- Are there any infra tweaks happening tonight that could confound results (gc, kernel upgrade)? Pinged #infra-alerts.
- Does dedicated infra for customer X have a different eviction policy? Need to check Dedicated defaults.

Random TODOs (personal):
- Add unit test for cache.set ttl default (5m) -> was failing with implicit 0.
- Clean up stray debug logs in kv_populate path before merging hotfix.
- Draft a short note for product on fallback plan: when kv hit rate low, auto-reduce batch_size to 4 and use faster model variant.

Meeting notes snippets (from stand / quick sync):
- Mina: trying eviction dampening, will push branch 'eviction-damp' by EOD.
- Diego: kernel scheduler counters now in the debug branch, need to wire to console for live dashboards.
- Product: they'd like an automatic safeguard for enterprise tenant Y to avoid p99 > 2s. Could be conservative batch cap + model variant fallback.

Things I want to remember tomorrow:
- Run Change B (router batch cap) first — cheapest risk.
- If p99 drops but p50 rises, check if it's due to more small batches (higher overhead).
- Ask infra for kernel dmesg from 2026-03-12 02:00-03:00 window.

Loose ideas (brainstorm):
- Adaptive prefix warming: if request path indicates low KV coverage, proactively warm first N tokens for next expected user requests (requires prediction heuristics).
- Greedy small-batch filler: for batches with mixed kv hits, pad cold entries with lightweight prefetch that returns partial token cache so runtime can start generation earlier.

Final micro-checklist (today):
- [ ] Add kv.miss_reason tag (quick patch)
- [ ] Run experiments A/B/C, collect traces
- [ ] Merge tiny ttl unit test
- [ ] Draft prod-notes for enterprise fallback plan

Notes to self: keep this doc super ephemeral. If anything stabilizes, move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/postmortems.

End of dump.
